submission.justification: D3 has the highest light yield (38 PE/MeV at 20%) but 30% of modules failed thermal cycling, against a 5% limit. Modules can't be repaired once the cryostat is filled, so D3 is excluded. D1 passes at 2% failures and gives more light than D2 (27 vs 18 PE/MeV at 20%). Light yield rises with coverage, and feedthroughs are available up to 30%, so I chose 30%. The coverage^0.8 scaling is an extrapolation from the 2025 simulation. It gives about 37 PE/MeV for D1 at 30%. I did not run a new simulation.

requirements.evidence: D1 is the highest-yield design that passes robustness. At 30% coverage it is estimated at about 37 PE/MeV (27 × 1.5^0.8), extrapolated from the 20% simulation.

requirements.requirement: Module is one of the three listed designs
Robust, since modules are inaccessible after filling (at most 5% failures after 20 thermal cycles)
requirements.evidence: D1 had 2% failures. D3 had 30% and D2 had 0.5%.
30% was chosen. The meeting notes say feedthroughs are enough for up to 30%.
